status: independent arithmetic, direct-row-enumeration and generated-certificate audit complete

validation.oracle_independence: Exhaustive nondecreasing positive integer partitions of R into <=M jobs; direct ceil(r_i*C/B) per partition. No wave interval/capacity DP used in oracle.

lemma_verdict: Correct under explicit ideal complete-row job assumptions. It is elementary integer packing, not a new theorem claim.
proof: Let B,C,M be positive integers, R a nonnegative integer, and RC=WB with integer W. There are at most M positive integer complete-row jobs (normally one job per chip), sum r_i=R, and independent cost w_i=ceil(r_i C/B).
The sum of nonnegative excesses sum_i(w_i-r_i C/B) equals sum_i w_i-W. Thus total W occurs iff every excess is zero, equivalently B divides r_i C for every job.
Write g=gcd(B,C), p=B/g and q=C/g, with gcd(p,q)=1. Then exact fill requires r_i=p t_i and w_i=q t_i for integer t_i>=0. RC=WB also implies R=pN and W=qN for an integer N.
For at most M jobs, max t_i is at least ceil(N/M). Balanced integer t_i attain it, proving D_exact=q ceil((W/q)/M). Exactly M nonempty jobs additionally require N>=M.
Without the exact-total-work restriction, max r_i>=ceil(R/M); monotonicity gives D_min=ceil(ceil(R/M) C/B). Distributing rows as evenly as possible attains it, including R<M and C>B.
For depth cap D alone, feasibility is exactly R<=M floor(DB/C). Every job can hold at most floor(DB/C) rows, and assigning rows up to that capacity is sufficient in this ideal job model.

The capacity-DP minimal-work witness is sound despite tracking upper endpoints only: if a minimum-work parent had sum of lower endpoints >R, delete rows from its maximum-capacity assignment until R remain. At least one job then falls to a cheaper wave interval, yielding a feasible smaller-work assignment and contradicting minimality. The code also materializes and checks the parent.

edge_cases.conclusion: D_min=D_exact=2 with one positive job; globally balanced waves [1,1,0,0] are not realizable. Original certificate() assert was a genuine optional-control bug, fixed by nullable balanced_wave_profile. Archived v1 and current execution reproduced in api_edge_regression.json.
W=3,q=3,N=1: one 2-row job achieves exact work at depth3; forcing both chips nonempty requires [1,1] rows, 4 waves total. The lemma assumes <=M positive jobs.

edge_cases.case: pooled ceiling is not exact pooled fill
edge_cases.conclusion: ceil(RC/B)=2 but RC/B=4/3. Two 1-row jobs cost one wave each, depth1; q=2 does not force individual wave costs to multiples of2. Do not use the exact-fill formula when RC%B!=0.
R=0 gives W=D_min=D_exact=0 arithmetically; the current positive-row compiler API deliberately excludes it.

edge_cases.case: number of jobs versus number of chips
edge_cases.conclusion: At most M jobs is the stated max-job-depth problem. If many serial jobs per chip are allowed, max-job-depth is a different metric; the same balancing expression can bound total waves per chip, not the depth of each tiny job.

physical_scope: A job starts at a legal wave-aligned full-row stream boundary, uses one original full input vector/dimension, and all coefficient bytes are counted. No wave can be jointly shared with another independent job in this cost model.

B is usable coefficient payload bytes in an ordinary full-plane read wave, not raw page+spare bytes. C must include any in-band row packing/alignment/scale bytes that consume NAND payload, or metadata must be separately costed. Input bytes, command bytes, output/FIFO bytes and controller time are separate costs.

All emitted 14-shape witnesses independently fit within one 192-wave block per job (largest112 waves). Fresh wave-aligned blocks establish this limited single-block feasibility; the module emits logical row bands, not dense multi-job physical addresses or a minimal-capacity FTL allocation.

For multi-block jobs, ceil(total coefficient bytes/B) is only an ideal lower bound unless legal whole-row splits preserve it. Example B2,C3,R2,M1 with block2waves: ideal3waves, but two full-row native calls each need2waves, total4. Footnote9 alone does not expose partial-row accumulator continuation.

The generic certificate capability object omits native input-buffer capacity, field widths and output behavior; each backend must additionally validate those limits. Independent LUNs, plane masks, contexts and page-buffer replay are not assumed.

opaque_row_numeric_contract.statement: For each desired output row j, native kernel computes F(original full row bytes, original full input bytes, original column order/dimension, original row/expert metadata, original arithmetic mode). F must be row-separable and independent of physical address/job row count except row selection. Moving intact rows and scattering outputs then calls the identical F for each j.
opaque_row_numeric_contract.proof: Each desired row is present exactly once and receives identical F arguments. Its opaque result therefore matches before/after placement. This is substitution of the same row function, not reassociation of a dot product; no raw-I32 return, output conversion, column partials or host reduction is needed.
must_preserve: Row scales/quantization groups/bias/original row index and padding/valid-length semantics
Native accumulator reset and full-row column sequence
Output quantization not dependent on all other rows in the current job, unless equivalent original global metadata is supplied
Padded or unwanted fringe outputs cannot affect desired row results, and must be drained/discarded under the native interface
opaque_row_numeric_contract.not_established_by_proof: Whether an actual unpublished AiF numeric implementation meets all these assumptions. It also does not preserve uncorrected location-dependent bit faults; the logical coefficient bytes must be the same.

fringe_output_contract.status: conditional inference from publicly described dimension/block/offset/page-count command, not a confirmed AiF PE behavior
fringe_output_contract.issue: If PE emits a full output for every C-byte row in all consumed padded pages, host must drain/discard surplus complete outputs. If a native valid-row cutoff exists, that cost can be avoided; the inspected paper does not expose it.
fringe_output_contract.cost_rule: Use sum floor(pages_i*page_bytes/C) for a page-count stream, or sum floor(waves_i*B/C) if all full-plane pages enter PE. Include extra output bytes/drain commands in matched layouts; no asserted output dtype.

interpretation: Qwen38 GU exactwork50 requires q5 jobs and least exactwork depth5, while minimum jobdepth4 needs at least51 totalwaves. Down exactwork25 requires depth5, while depth2 needs26.

G4 GU exactwork24 requires depth3 versus least depth2 requiring25waves; Deep down44 requires depth11 versus least depth3 requiring45waves. This explains why minimum total work and minimum per-job depth differ.

No depth gap does not mean no placement opportunity: Granite3 down exactwork8 versus equal16 has capacity undersaturation at unchanged depth1; subgroup/query scheduling remains a separate tradeoff. Mixtral down q7 but D_min56 is already a multiple of7.

Whole-row numeric compatibility and physical certificates may be useful system contributions when paired with a nontrivial lowering/runtime and gains against all-width unequal-row/standard integer-packing matched controls; the lemma/DP, hardware-aware tiling or complement assignment alone are not novelty claims.
targeted_prior_verdict: No inspected primary directly duplicates the precise ordinary-NAND whole-row work/depth frontier plus opaque-row numeric and physical lowering certificate. Cambricon is a direct strong flash-tiling prior; NVIDIA/Felix establish generic quantization/divisibility/compiler principles. This is a bounded negative finding, not publication novelty certification.
